blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: D-type flip-flop — A circuit that stores one bit.
D input — The data value presented to the flip-flop.
trigger — The clock event that causes sampling.
Q output — The currently stored bit.

blocks.title: Why do we need flip-flops?
blocks.text: Logic gates calculate; a flip-flop remembers. Registers must hold values even when other inputs change.

blocks.title: Meet the D-type flip-flop
blocks.text: D is the data input. Q is the stored output. CLK determines when Q can update.

blocks.title: Supermarket door analogy
blocks.text: D can change before the sample. Q only stores the new value at CLK ↑.

blocks.title: Digital watch: divide by two
blocks.text: NOT Q fed into D causes Q to toggle at each rising edge.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model when Q changes — and when it holds
blocks.text: Q initially stores 1 . Follow CLK first, then D, then Q. Watch what happens at a falling edge, when D changes alone, and at each rising edge.

questions.prompt: Choose the response that best addresses this independent task: Trace four rising clock edges Q initially stores 1. Predict its value at each rising edge (↑).
questions.answer: CHECK · EDGE 4 D = 1 → Q = 1 Q becomes 1. Record row 4 and review the complete waveform.
options: THE RULE Sample on ↑, hold otherwise A rising clock edge makes Q copy D. Q visibly changes only if the sampled D differs from its stored value. A falling edge or a change in D alone never updates this rising-edge-triggered flip-flop.
